investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes is fully consumed. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, which restrict remote-agent pods to the kata/peer-pod capable node pool. Preemption was also exhausted: no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled within the eval's timeout window (~136–146 s), the runner received no VM ID and no remoteState, causing all required evidence to be absent and all three checks to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked/zombie pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to the kata/peer-pod node pool; the 4 remaining nodes are ineligible by configuration, so capacity cannot be borrowed from the general pool.

[Possible] A peer-pod VM leak or stuck agent from a prior eval run is holding a VM slot on one or both eligible nodes, preventing the new pod from being scheduled even though the agent is no longer active.

[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node is set too low relative to concurrent eval demand — if multiple eval runs or user workloads compete for the same 2-node pool simultaneously, slots exhaust quickly.
[Lower confidence] A node in the kata pool may have become NotReady or cordoned between runs, reducing effective capacity from a previously larger pool to just 2 nodes.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 15:42 and 15:47 UTC on 2026-06-27 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested kata.peerpods.io/vm pods because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state for ~136–150 s before the eval times out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval suite for the remote-agents feature.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes is fully consumed. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, which restrict remote-agent pods to the kata/peer-pod capable node pool. Preemption was also exhausted: no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled within the eval's timeout window (~136–146 s), the runner received no VM ID and no remoteState, causing all required evidence to be absent and all three checks to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked/zombie pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to the kata/peer-pod node pool; the 4 remaining nodes are ineligible by configuration, so capacity cannot be borrowed from the general pool.

[Possible] A peer-pod VM leak or stuck agent from a prior eval run is holding a VM slot on one or both eligible nodes, preventing the new pod from being scheduled even though the agent is no longer active.

[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node is set too low relative to concurrent eval demand — if multiple eval runs or user workloads compete for the same 2-node pool simultaneously, slots exhaust quickly.
[Lower confidence] A node in the kata pool may have become NotReady or cordoned between runs, reducing effective capacity from a previously larger pool to just 2 nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-27T15:42–15:47Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to help. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response evidence, causing a total contract gap (all 5 required fields — orgId, agentId, model, provider, message — are missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity or selector constraints at all. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~136–150 s), preventing the eval from reaching the agent runtime and producing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId, meaning pod scheduling is the first blocking operation before any evidence can be collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared pod scheduling layer is the common failure point.
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the VM-backed peer-pod slots are fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is the strongest explanation given the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message across all three sibling checks.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall on those 2 nodes.
Cluster node pool under-provisioning: the total node count (6) with only 2 affinity-eligible nodes may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, causing contention.

Peer-pod VM quota limit at the infrastructure or cloud provider level: an external quota cap on kata peer-pod VMs could prevent new VMs from being allocated even if Kubernetes believes capacity exists.
Transient spike in remote-agent workloads consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run, which may self-resolve if workloads complete.

reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (e.g., kubectl describe node) to check the allocatable and allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm counts on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. Confirm whether slots are fully consumed.

reproductionSteps.details: Confirm which label selectors or affinity rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of the 6 nodes, and verify whether those 4 excluded nodes could be made eligible.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1913–1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers peer-pod scheduling. The pod never became schedulable, so no evidence was collected and the contract failed entirely (expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

recommendedNextActions: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm resource utilization on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes immediately to confirm exhaustion and identify which workloads are holding slots.
Determine whether any remote-agent pods from previous eval runs or production workloads are stuck in a non-terminating state and consuming VM slots; force-delete any leaked pods if found.

Assess whether the node pool serving remote agents needs to be scaled out (more nodes with the required affinity labels and kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity) to handle concurrent eval and production load.

Review the pod affinity/selector rules for remote-agent pods to determine whether the 4 currently ineligible nodes could be made eligible by adding the required labels, increasing effective capacity from 2 to up to 6 nodes.
Investigate whether a cloud provider or infrastructure-level quota cap on peer-pod VMs is preventing new VM allocation even when Kubernetes reports capacity.

Once the scheduling issue is resolved, re-run all three remote-agents checks and confirm that orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message evidence are returned and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.
Consider adding a cluster-level alert on kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization approaching 100% on affinity-eligible nodes so this condition is detected before evals fail.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is ongoing or was transient. A pass would return orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message evidence; a fail with the same Unschedulable message confirms persistent capacity exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies that all three checks share the same scheduling failure root cause and that no partial recovery has occurred.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and allocated capacity on all 6 cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly proves or disproves the resource exhaustion hypothesis and identifies whether the 4 non-matching nodes could be made eligible.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe nodes and filter for kata.peerpods.io/vm to see current allocatable vs. allocated counts per node, and confirm which 2 nodes match the pod affinity.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether exhaustion is from active workloads, leaked eval pods, or a quota cap, which determines the remediation path.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Query the cluster for all pods requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to identify what is consuming the available slots and whether any are stuck or leaked.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run a local-agent check to confirm the failure is isolated to the remote peer-pod path
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If local-agent-create passes, it confirms the API, auth, and org resolution layers are healthy and the failure is specific to the kata peer-pod scheduling path used by remote agents.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A subsequent eval run where remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime succeeds and returns evidence (orgId, agentId, etc.) would indicate the scheduling failure was transient and capacity has recovered.
kubectl describe node output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.
A different failure message (e.g., authentication error, API timeout, or network error) on a re-run would indicate the root cause is not pod scheduling but a different layer.
Evidence that the 4 non-matching nodes were recently reconfigured or had their labels/taints changed would shift the diagnosis toward a node affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

Passing results from local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime checks (which do not use kata peer-pods) would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/peer-pod scheduling path and not a broader API or auth issue.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm available capacity on the remote-agent node pool before attempting agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct, earlier signal.
Add a pod scheduling latency eval that alerts when a remote-agent pod takes longer than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s) to reach Running state, catching capacity pressure before full exhaustion.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 of 6), catching node pool shrinkage or label drift.

Add a sibling-correlation eval rule that automatically escalates to a shared-dependency investigation when all checks under a feature fail with structurally identical scheduler messages within the same run window.
